record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: How does thermal friction from gluon scattering modify the dynamics of QCD axion strings, and can that friction leave observable signatures or substantially change the predicted axion number abundance produced by the string network?

evidence.quote: Another aspect of the string network that needs to be explored carefully is the affect of friction on the string network. QCD axion strings have large geometric scattering cross sections with gluons and thus the thermal plasma provides an important source of friction for axion strings [103]. When the scaling solution is found numerically, the thermal bath is ignored and thus these important friction terms are neglected. It would be interesting if this friction term had any observable consequences or changed the predicted axion number abundance.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has begun to quantitatively address this question. Studies of axion dark matter with thermal friction (e.g., 2206.01462) and a 2026 analysis "Putting the Brakes on Axion Strings: Friction and Its Impact on the QCD Axion Abundance" (arXiv:2603.00237) compute friction effects from gluon scattering on QCD axion strings, finding that friction delays the onset of scaling, reduces near-QCD-epoch velocities, and reshapes the infrared part of the axion emission spectrum, though the gluon-induced friction at the QCD epoch is found to be subdominant in some regimes. The question is therefore partially solved: friction has been modeled and its qualitative impact identified, but a definitive determination of observable consequences and the precise change to the predicted axion abundance remains an active area of investigation.

status_evidence.title: Putting the Brakes on Axion Strings: Friction and Its Impact on the QCD Axion Abundance
status_evidence.snippet: Friction delays the onset of scaling, reduces typical velocities near the QCD epoch, and reshapes the infrared part of the emission.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative study showing friction modifies scaling and reshapes axion emission, partially answering the question.

status_evidence.title: Axion dark matter with thermal friction
status_evidence.snippet: Thermal friction allows QCD axions much lighter than microeV to be viable without tuning the initial misalignment angle.
status_evidence.claim: Thermal friction can substantially modify cosmological axion abundance predictions.
